yaw_isolation.method: 20 s, 400 samples, calm environment, constant normalized port/starboard commands [-0.5,+0.5], identical shared 0.35 s actuator lag
yaw_isolation.moment_arm_serialization: matched: Node NED y=[-0.33,+0.33] maps to Gazebo FLU y=[+0.33,-0.33]
yaw_isolation.finding: Yaw sign and moment arm are correct. Steady rate differs by only 1.9%; the accumulated angle difference is consistent with that small persistent rate offset. The former 7.8 rad raw statistic also crossed the +/-pi serialization boundary and was not a circular angle metric.
yaw_isolation.action: No yaw coefficient or physics change made. The isolation result does not justify tuning nR/nRR or changing thruster placement.

current.frame_mapping: NED [N,E] -> Gazebo ENU [E,N]; Gazebo FLU lateral velocity is the negative of Node body-starboard velocity
current.relative_velocity_sign: matched: both evaluate hull velocity minus current for damping
current.correction: VRX adds damping(v-current)-damping(v) because SimpleHydrodynamics already applies damping(v)
current.source_result: no sign or frame defect found

wind.defect_found: Stock vrx::USVWind applies independent X/Y quadratic drag in world coordinates and does not rotate Surveyor frontal/side projected areas with hull heading. Its coeff_vector is therefore not a serialization of Node WindLoad for a turning anisotropic craft.
wind.equation: Transform wind-world minus hull-world velocity into body coordinates; Fx=0.5*rho*Cd*A_front*speed*u_rel and Fy=0.5*rho*Cd*A_side*speed*v_rel; rotate force back to ENU.

prescribed_velocity_test.result: exact agreement to 1e-12 for relative body velocity and world force after NED/ENU and starboard/left conversion
prescribed_velocity_test.negative_control: stock USVWind world-axis formula diverges for an oblique heading

post_fix_short_isolation.interpretation: The corrected combined force direction now agrees essentially exactly. Magnitude remains 34.3% high, slightly outside the preregistered 30% band, and the current-only response accounts for most of the combined displacement and residual scale error. The very small wind-only displacement makes its angle sensitive to millimetre-scale settling differences.

verification.full_gate_7_rerun: not run; the short corrected response remains outside tolerance

next_evidence_needed: A prescribed-force or planar-constraint comparison is needed to separate the remaining current-response scale difference from VRX 3D hull motion before any damping coefficient is changed.
